understanding the barriers to suicide intervention in people with substance disorders in South Africa.
the role of mental health care providers in suicide prevention in South Africa.
the social determinants of suicide and how these may be addressed in the context of substance use disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the responsibility for prevention of suicide in people with a substance use disorder is not the responsibility of one stakeholder but rather a collaborative effort of multiple stakeholders.

mental health care providers perceive structural, social, economic, and contextual barriers to suicide prevention among people with substance use disorder in Cape Town, and that these barriers need to be considered when planning suicide prevention strategies in South Africa.

suicide prevention interventions should be tailored to address the needs of people with substance use and should take into account contextual factors that may serve as barriers to effective suicide prevention.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mental health care providers in this study thought that the barriers to suicide were so numerous and so difficult to overcome that suicide prevention in this population was impossible.
we have identified the barriers to suicide in people with a substance use disorder and have identified how we can overcome those barriers.
the barriers to suicide in people with SUD are not just about individual risk factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
suicide is a complex phenomenon and requires a multifaceted response that addresses individual, structural, and contextual factors.
the responsibility for preventing suicide in people who have substance use disorders should not be placed on mental health care providers alone.
suicide prevention interventions should be designed to address contextual factors and the social determinants of health.
